patches.title: Split fused tool-call arguments into separate calls
patches.symptom: a tool call fails with `Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON` because the relay streamed two calls into one index
patches.rootCause: pi-ai parseToolCallArguments throws MALFORMED_RESPONSE on the concatenation and dsh-agent-loop re-throws it because it is absent from retryableCodes (dsh-llm-pi-ai/lib/index.js:1656, upstream #4427; the chain is in its doc)
limits: cannot recover a call whose tail was cut by max-tokens (finish.reason.kind === length)
does not fix the relay or adapter that assigned one index to two calls
does not reorder or rename calls; the first call keeps the original id

patches.title: A rescue must be provable, attributable and atomic
patches.symptom: a split-out call could run under an empty or wrong tool name, replay without replayState, or commit before a later block of the same stream was rejected
patches.rootCause: block-end repairs committed as they arrived, one name per index, and stop emitted without replayState: the JSON proof held while the call could still be dispatched wrong
limits: on rc.1 the adapter never closed a tool-call block; on rc.3 it closes the first fragment and leaves the surplus to the finish path
a synthesized block-start is proven on the finish path only (BS-11); a two-tool fusion sends the surplus out as remedy_unattributed (BS-18)
a tool name that arrives twice with different values stays unrepairable

patches.title: A refusal must be observable, and a withdrawal must not read as a repair
patches.symptom: a stream whose only defect is plain bad JSON read "repair incomplete", and a withdrawn repair was indistinguishable from a fusion nobody could split
patches.rootCause: recordRejected incremented fused and unrepaired for every rejection whatever its code, so a refusal that never proved a fusion inflated fused — the difference between "we declined" and "we could not" was erased
limits: the four verdict states and their order are unchanged: the counts are reported, never judged
no state name can say "observed, refused, and correctly not repaired"; only the counter row carries it
old journal lines keep the six-field shape: no migration rewrites them

patches.title: A bare value after a member key must be resealed, or refused — never guessed
patches.symptom: a tool call fails with `Unexpected token` or `Unexpected end of JSON input` because the model wrote a program, not a JSON string, after `"code":`
patches.rootCause: a bare unquoted multi-line blob as one member value is neither a fusion nor splittable, so P-0001 refused it as `single-object` and the call never dispatched
limits: reseals only when exactly one member value proves; two possible resealings is refused as ambiguous
never touches a truncated call; a duplicate key, doubled colon, missing brace or illegal escape stays a refusal
keeps the call id: no synthetic identity, and the stream budget is untouched

patches.title: A second seam with no test is a seam nobody has ever run
patches.symptom: agent/request-error shipped in 0.2.0 behind retryOnMalformed with zero tests, and was wrong three ways: it called next() then overrode the answer, never pruned its budget Map, and would have retried image-offload and credential failures
patches.rootCause: the listener was written against an assumed contract: a handling listener returns {kind:"retry"} without calling next(), and a waterfall listener that does not own the decision must return next()
limits: only MALFORMED_RESPONSE is retried; SERVER, TRANSPORT and TIMEOUT already self-heal upstream, so a second layer would compete
the retry budget defaults to 0: nothing is retried unless a deployment asks for it
the bound is 256 cache entries; an evicted entry lets a very long turn spend a fresh retry
the live artifact is a synthetic endpoint: it reproduces the adapter failure, not a relay incident

patches.title: One byte cap for two load paths is a cap that taxes the wrong half
patches.symptom: one 68000-byte ceiling counted a mounted plugin and a CLI invocation as the same thing; P-0011 needed 4 263 bytes that did not fit, and paying meant deleting prose a daemon loads
patches.rootCause: gate_size summed every emitted module into one number and never asked which of them a running plugin imports: the CLI-only half sat beside the bytes that load on every session
limits: the caps are recorded, not assumed: they moved twice in one session with the owner signature (budgets.mjs)
the lists are explicit; the test reads only the relative import graph, so a dynamic import is not caught
a split budget cannot tell good growth from bad, only which half pays
it caps emitted JavaScript only, not declarations, fixtures or package-root files

patches.title: The failure class this host hits most after fusion was named by nobody
patches.symptom: 37 turns on this host died with UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT (one sentence, three workspaces, eleven sessions) while the resident layer said nothing; INVALID_REQUEST, MISSING_CREDENTIAL and EMPTY_RESPONSE were silent too
patches.rootCause: the refusal is thrown during preparation, before any stream exists: it reaches agent/error, not llm/stream or agent/request-error, and no listener was on it
limits: naming is always on, never repairs or retries: one named line instead of one dead turn
preflight is a pure decision, not a mount: nothing wires it into agent/pre-step yet
a refused level is reported with a suggestion, never silently downgraded
a model whose metadata lives only in the adapter reads unknown, never assumed

patches.title: A scan must read the log it is pointed at, and a redaction must see every path shape
patches.symptom: `dsh-remedy scan <session.v4.jsonl.zstd>` reported 0 attempts and one unreadable line per compressed byte, and artifacts citing a session carried the account name in three shapes the redactor could not match
patches.rootCause: cmdScan read a multi-frame zstd log with readFileSync(file, "utf8") instead of the decompressSessionLog reader the plugin ships, and core/redact.ts matched only a single-backslash C:\Users\<name>
limits: a filtered scan reports before_since instead of guessing; an unstamped event is unreadable, never assumed in the window
one undecompressable file is a failure line and exit 3, not a silent zero
it does not deduplicate a repair seen by both the journal and the session file
matches a home path only when the directory starts with a drive letter; another spelling is unmeasured

patches.title: A scan that counts only the repairable turns is not a fault map
patches.symptom: `scan` reported 44 fusion failures of 287 finished turns; the 88 `max-tokens` and 36 `UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT` turns were counted nowhere
patches.rootCause: session-scan.ts returned early on `kind !== "error"` and on `code !== "MALFORMED_RESPONSE"`: a filter for "can this layer repair it" carried into a map of "how the turn ended"
limits: reported, never promoted: the exit code still turns on fused_calls and fusion_failures
truncated turns stay unfixed; fusion_failures keeps its exact MALFORMED_RESPONSE meaning
a reason.kind this census does not know is left uncounted, not bucketed

patches.title: A copy channel that reports "exited null" cannot be repaired
patches.symptom: the two longest outward files could not be regenerated at all: every attempt printed `agy exited null`, so two different faults had one unreadable name
patches.rootCause: the request (35509 chars for changelog, 33530 for readme) exceeded the 32767-character Windows command line, so spawnSync failed with ENAMETOOLONG and a null status; a spawn killed by the timeout reported the same null. Transport is now chosen by request length
limits: no retry across transports: it picks one from the request length and reports the failure
the timeout is raised to half an hour, not removed; a failure is diagnosed, never repaired
the fact pack is not shortened to fit: argv only serves the smallest briefs

patches.title: A byte budget that no script checks is a suggestion
patches.symptom: the byte budget was crossed three times in three consecutive patches (55815, 64539, 70389) and every crossing was found by hand after the build
patches.rootCause: the caps lived only in the fact pack and README.md; nothing under scripts/ read them, so a patch that crossed a line stayed green through the whole suite
limits: the gate measures the emitted plugin only: core does not load at startup, so the ceiling protects what is loaded there
it does not shrink anything; the measured numbers stay what they were when the gate was written
it does not measure dist/*.d.ts, which is paid at build time rather than load time
it cannot decide how to split a file that crosses a cap: it only refuses the crossing

patches.title: The npm page documented a CLI that had not existed since 0.3.3
patches.symptom: packages/plugin/README.md (the page npm renders) and the CLI USAGE disagreed about what scan accepts, and neither admitted a directory, --since or --max-files, all shipped by P-0004
patches.rootCause: nothing watched either string: gate_copy covers the root outward files, the package README had no output_sha256 and no gate, and no test compared the two strings, so a red result was impossible
limits: the gate set still does not cover packages/*/README.md: the test compares the two scan lines, not the page as a whole
moving the page into the copy channel would make it generated, which is a separate decision
the one-line-per-command rewrite pays for the flag list, so the per-command prose is thinner; the detail lives in the patch document

patches.title: A windowed scan called the one dated line every session starts with unreadable
patches.symptom: `scan --since` reported one unreadable line per file read: 78 files gave 78 unreadable lines while every byte of them parsed, so the tool said "I could not read this" about the one line every session starts with
patches.rootCause: `session-scan.ts` required a numeric `time` before applying the window and counted anything else as unreadable; the `session` header carries `createdAt`, not `time`, so every header fell into that branch
limits: only the `session` header is dated by createdAt; an event with no instant stays unreadable, because there is no second field to fall back to
a header inside the window adds its instant but no attempts or turns, so the census does not move

patches.title: The project describing itself is the part nothing checked
patches.symptom: the fact pack pinned core 0.3.7 and called 0.3.6 the previous release while 0.3.8 shipped, quoted a hash no file hashed to, and the npm page documented four commands after explain shipped
patches.rootCause: the copy criterion checked the shape of a number and never the pack own statements; gate_ssot read data/results/*.json but never a hash printed in prose; cli-usage.test.ts compared one line
limits: the package README is still hand-written prose: USAGE is its guard, not a hash (BS-13 narrows)
the pack is checked only against other repository files; a claim nothing else records stays unverified
the hash check skips any evidence row that compares two publishes instead of guessing
gate_copy cannot see the handoff or the package README: those are governance tests, not gates

patches.title: The seam nobody mounted because nobody measured what refusing looks like
patches.symptom: agent/pre-step stayed unmounted on one sentence repeated in three places: "a rejected step opens no step, but what the user sees has not been measured"; a seam that can refuse before a token was blocked by an unchecked assumption
patches.rootCause: the claim was never run; the loop source answers it: preStep awaits the waterfall and, on a reject, closes the turn with reason "blocked" and no step
limits: it measures the seam, it does not mount a product on it: nothing calls agent/pre-step in a shipped profile
the desktop UI render of reason.kind "blocked" stays unmeasured, and the probe ran headless only
a rejection discards the claimed input: the user retypes the message, so an enter decision is the better default
only the first proposed step of one turn was exercised

patches.title: The command that answers "what covers this" kept its own copy of the answer
patches.symptom: `explain` answered "what covers this class" from its own COVERAGE and SWITCHES constants, so the registry and the command were two homes for one claim and nothing compared them
patches.rootCause: the command predates the registry carrying that claim; its local tables were the only map a user read, and a human diff by eye was the only mechanism
limits: moves six claims and no behaviour: the printed table is identical before and after
switch keys stay a closed vocabulary (repair, retryOnMalformed); another key must be added, not inferred
a covered-but-unmounted patch still reads covered-and-off: coverage is a claim about the code

patches.title: The two pages npm renders had no mechanism at all
patches.symptom: both package pages are hand-written with no output_sha256 and no copy-channel entry, so gate_copy never saw them; 2331 bytes of the plugin page was compared against nothing while being what a stranger installs from
patches.rootCause: the copy channel was built for the repository-root files, and the package pages predate it; each round pinned one more line instead of answering what else was unguarded
limits: proves no prose number and no undispatchable command can rot; layout and behavioural claims stay hand-written
the number rule is the copy channel criterion, not a truth test, so a page can still describe absent behaviour
core/README.md is held to the weaker half only: it documents a library, not a command

patches.title: A Windows exit code printed as a bare number sent an operator hunting the wrong cause
patches.symptom: the publish wrapper printed "npm exited 3221226505" and HTTP-shaped advice, so the operator hunted a credentials problem; that number is Windows 0xC0000409
patches.rootCause: npmFailureAdvice only understands HTTP codes; a process killed by the Windows runtime has no HTTP answer and fell through to the generic branch
limits: names only the two codes this machine produced (0xC0000409, 0xC0000005); another Windows exception still prints raw
does not retry the publish: the advice tells the operator to run the direct call
cannot prove the crash was the runtime rather than npm; it proves no HTTP request was logged
no live artifact is possible: this is advice printed by a build script

patches.title: The page strangers read first described a project that had stopped existing
patches.symptom: README.md and README.zh-CN.md described a single-wrapper project of eighteen patches, and repeated that agent/pre-step was unmeasured
patches.rootCause: gate_copy guards numbers, not shape: it checks that every prose digit exists in the fact pack and never whether the page still describes the product
limits: the root README still has no structural guard: a page could describe behaviour the code does not have (BS-13 own family)
it does not change what npm renders until a release carries the new pages
no live artifact: these are pages, not a seam

patches.title: A listing that pins git bytes while advertising a registry version installs neither
patches.symptom: docs/market-index.json declared version 0.3.8 and a git commit in one entry, and that commit carried nineteen patches while 0.3.8 ships thirteen
patches.rootCause: the guard checked the shape of the pin and never its meaning: any hex commit passed, so every document commit forced a re-pin
limits: it does not turn the repository into a published artifact: the patches it names stay merged and unreleased
a git source needs an explicit unreleased marker; "newest" is a fact read at release time, not checked over the network
it fixes the index this project publishes; a third party that already read this repository is out of reach

patches.title: The published package advertised a subpath that never had a module
patches.symptom: the manifest exported "./retry-listener" -> ./dist/retry-listener.js, a module that has never existed (the second seam is failure-listener.ts), so the import answered ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND while the manifest promised it; it shipped in 0.3.8 and 0.4.0
patches.rootCause: the test compared the target string against a regex and never the file behind it, so a plausible path passed as well as a real one
limits: it checks the source tree, not the packed tarball: a module excluded by files would still pass
it does not check main or bin against src/, although both are pinned by the same test file
it does not check that an exported subpath is documented, or that a documented subpath is exported

patches.title: The drift test repaired the drift before it looked for it
patches.symptom: tests/unit/fixtures-sync.test.ts ran sync_fixtures.mjs in write mode and then compared the copy, so the copy step overwrote any drift before the assertion ran; the read-only --check mode existed but no consumer used it
patches.rootCause: the test was written as setup plus assertion and the setup was the same operation it claimed to verify, so the negative control had nowhere to run
limits: prepack still runs write mode: packing has to create the copy, only the test is read-only first
the negative control corrupts one fixture; a drift that changes the file set is handled by --check but not exercised
the --source/--target/--checksums flags are a test seam and nothing pins them beyond this test file

patches.title: The workflow first step was a sentence nobody read
patches.symptom: AGENTS.md says every patch starts with a doc, but gate_registry resolved only evidence and guards: at the start of R31 the registry held twenty-one patches and docs/patches held nineteen, P-0016 among the missing, while every check stayed green
patches.rootCause: the doc was read as prose about the patch rather than as part of it: evidence and guards are paths the gate resolves, so a doc in neither list could be missing with no check noticing
limits: it checks that a doc exists, not that it is true: a doc can still describe behaviour the code does not have
it matches by id prefix, which is safe only while ids stay P-NNNN
an orphan doc with no registry entry is not reported, because the gate iterates the registry rather than the directory
no live artifact is possible: this is a governance gate

patches.title: The two pages npm renders were outside the copy channel
patches.symptom: both package READMEs were hand-written and absent from docs/copy/manifest.json, so gate_copy never checked their bytes, fact-pack hash or writer
patches.rootCause: the copy channel was defined as "the outward files at the repository root", so the two package pages were read as package metadata rather than as the first thing a stranger opens
limits: the copy gate checks numbers, bytes and provenance, not truth: a page can still describe behaviour the code does not have
the pages ship inside the tarball, so a change reaches npm only with a release
the pages stay hand-written prose that is now registered; a generated page is a separate decision

patches.title: An unread profile was reported as a finding
patches.symptom: `explain --sessions <dir>` printed `(no)` in the "enabled here" cell for every covered class and exited 1, while its footer said the answer was unknown without a profile
patches.rootCause: `enabled` had two states where the domain has three: `isPatchOn` answered false for a null config, so "nobody read a profile" became "every coverer is switched off" and `uncovered` counted it into the exit code
limits: covers "no profile was read"; a profile read without a switch key still falls back to the default, unmeasured
exit 0 without a profile means "nothing found", not "nothing wrong": pass --profile-file for the old strictness
the row is tested, not the column widths: a longer patch id still shifts the layout

patches.title: The release procedure had two homes, and the older one was retired
patches.symptom: docs/PUBLISH.md described the real procedure while the handoff still sent a successor down the retired pnpm-filter path and told them to expect OTP, and its boundary section named a 0.3.5 tarball
patches.rootCause: handoff-truth checked the status table and the first thing; the release procedure lives after the evidence index, so it was outside the live contract while still being what a successor acts on
limits: the test pins the shape of the sections, not the truth of every step
it forbids the retired commands by pattern, so a differently worded wrong command is not caught
the boundary rule looks for .tmp/ paths and a `latest` version; a stale line phrased without either is still unread

patches.title: A fragment dispatched under a name nobody proved
patches.symptom: a fused text gluing two different tools sent the surplus call as the first tool`s name (INVALID_ARGS, measured twice on rc.3)
patches.rootCause: the rescue proves the JSON split and nothing else; the stream names one tool per index and the engine reused it for every fragment
limits: the proof needs a required list, a closed schema, or a declared value that breaks its own type; an open schema books the residue
the fallback name is not a tool, so the model pays one UNKNOWN_TOOL round trip: the cost of not running the wrong tool
a fragment that satisfies the wrong tool schema is still dispatched as that tool; a schema is a filter
the declarations come from options.tools; a hand-built call carries none

patches.title: A published sample carried this machine's home path
patches.symptom: every tarball since 0.1.0 shipped a fixture whose fused arguments carried the real workspace path, and the repository carried that account name in six patch docs, the handoff, a step review and one artifact (reported upstream on 2026-11-14)
patches.rootCause: redaction was wired into the artifact writers and never into the fixture corpus; P-0004 fixed the reader for three path shapes, not the files already tracked
limits: the fixture now carries <home>, so it is no longer a byte-for-byte copy; its note says so
the rule forbids an absolute Users/ segment; another shape is caught only by the P-0004 redactor
docs and artifacts were rewritten in place with unchanged stamps: a repair, not a re-measurement

patches.title: The pointers a successor acts on were prose nobody compared
patches.symptom: the live handoff called v0.4.2 the newest release after 0.4.5 shipped, its five-minute check still said "# 0.4.1", and PUBLISH.md said npm was at 0.4.2, while every gate stayed green
patches.rootCause: no rule compared a live version claim with package.json or the byte row: handoff-truth read the evidence index, release-procedure the command shapes, gate_size only the caps
limits: offline: the row is compared with package.json, not npm, so it can name a tag nobody published
the release body was compared by hand, which is not a mechanism
the channel rows in docs/distribution/README.md are dated readings no test reads

patches.title: The name check read required and nothing else, and its counter was a running total
patches.symptom: a declaration with no required list proved nothing, so a fragment kept the stream name even when its schema rejected it; and one repair's unattributed count landed on every later repair in the same stream ([1,1] instead of [1,0])
patches.rootCause: the check was written against an imagined schema: dsh-tools never sets additionalProperties (dsh-tools/lib/index.js:800-808), so an undeclared key is not proof; the counter bug was a scoping mistake above the per-decision loop
limits: an open schema cannot prove a fragment foreign by its keys, which is every first-party tool
fits is not identity: a fragment valid for the named tool is still dispatched as that tool
only the dsh-tools dialect was read; another dialect reads unproven more often, the safe direction

patches.title: The engine every mount loads had no budget, and a comment said it did
patches.symptom: P-0012 said core sits outside the size gate and a governance test claimed the package has "its own budget"; no cap existed anywhere, and by R41 the engine every mount loads had reached 98 247 emitted bytes
patches.rootCause: the budget predates the 0.4.0 split, which added a second package without a second measurement; "its own budget" described a plan, not a file
limits: the cap covers emitted core JavaScript only: .d.ts, fixtures and package-root files are outside it
it caps the total and the registry file, not each of the other nine modules
core is still not part of residency: the startup account is two rows read together
the cap forces a decision (split the registry, or sign a raise) rather than fixing a defect once

patches.title: The ledger carried the narrative its patch docs already carried
patches.symptom: the eight longest records measured 2 107-2 377 bytes each while the registry had 1 697 bytes left, so the next patch could not be recorded without a raise disguised as a split
patches.rootCause: the registry and docs/patches/ were both written in long form, so symptom, mechanism and limits existed twice while the code reads only the ledger fields
limits: the batch compacts 8 of 31 records; the rest keep their long form until touched
the 68 000 registry cap did not move: measured 66 303 before and 61 509 after
no per-record threshold was added: that needs the owner signature PROJECT_RULES section 1 requires
the prose removed is safe only while its doc says it, and gate_registry checks a doc exists (BS-19)

patches.title: A tool call with no identity was refused and then dispatched anyway
patches.symptom: a block whose id and name were both empty (measured `0.2.2-rc.3`, #13211) was counted as refused and passed through, so the host persisted a call with an empty callId and the V4 session could never resume
patches.rootCause: the block-end rejection path was written for fusion refusals, where passing the original through fails the turn visibly; an identity refusal does not fail visibly: it persists a call the host cannot dispatch
limits: the adapter that emits an incomplete call is not fixed: this seam names it and keeps the session resumable
a block that is both fused and empty is refused before any split (missing-id fires first)
the verdict stays quiet: the rejected event is the only record
arguments that parse to a non-object are untouched (the other half of #12064)

patches.title: A failed stream that no refusal explained was booked as a quiet one
patches.symptom: a turn ended with MALFORMED_RESPONSE and the journal booked nothing: no `errors`, no `refused`, no event (upstream #11337: a reasoning block, then an unsupported stop reason, turn dies)
patches.rootCause: `isFusionFailure` read the code alone, so every MALFORMED_RESPONSE inherited the fusion path's assumption that a refusal had already booked it
limits: the adapter is not fixed: `stopReason()` still rejects `refusal`, so the turn still ends; this seam names it
the verdict is untouched, so `quiet` still means the fusion defect was not seen
the reproduction is synthetic at the seam; the host half is the shipped `stopReason()` source

patches.title: A patch-layer row promised a module nothing resolved
patches.symptom: every `name:` in `cordis.patch.yml` promises an importable module and neither this repository nor the host checks before load time; #12318 shows the cost: `never started`, every resume fails
patches.rootCause: the namespace gate checked the shape of the rows but never resolved one against the exports it points into, so a rename in `src/` was only caught by a stranger installing the tarball
limits: it proves a row resolves, not that the host loads it
a declared package is accepted, which is not proof of its subpath
it runs in the suite, not at load time

patches.title: The host erased the id a delta-only stream had proved
patches.symptom: a delta-only tool call assembled as `id: ""` and the session could not resume (upstream #8653)
patches.rootCause: assembler.ts:72 assigns toolCallId unguarded while :73 guards the name, and :115 falls back only from null
limits: the host is not fixed; a different real id on one index passes through, so id-collision-split stays open
not verified: the red is at the seam, no live turn this round produced the shape

patches.title: One dropped closing delimiter killed the turn, and no proof was tried
patches.symptom: a nested argument one `]` short (upstream #12819: expected "," or "]" after an array element, three times in one session) was refused as `single-object` and re-thrown, so the whole turn died
patches.rootCause: the single-object branch had two outcomes, a proven reseal or a refusal, and a text one delimiter from parsing was neither; the splitter never saw it (`unbalanced: input ends at depth 1`)
limits: pi-ai route only: dsh-llm-deepseek reports "tool input is invalid JSON" without the text, so nothing reaches this seam
a missing final delimiter and an ambiguous text are refused, never guessed
verified on Linux (WSL2) against a scripted provider, not on a real model turn: the repair and the dispatch are live, the shape is synthesized

patches.title: The redaction was written on one platform and shipped to three
patches.symptom: a macOS or Linux home path went through `redact()` untouched: 5 of the 8 measured shapes (`/Users/<name>`, `file:///Users/<name>`, `--Users-…`, `--home-…`) left the account name in an artifact
patches.rootCause: two rules each assumed a Windows drive letter, and the session key is built by `projectKey`, which turns every separator into `-`: one project encodes three ways and only the Windows one matched
limits: the three shapes are tested as strings, not produced on their own platform, so this is not "tested on macOS"
/root/ is deliberately not redacted: the account name is the same string for everyone
the plugin itself stays platform-independent; only the evidence layer had a platform assumption
build scripts keep their WINDOWS branch on purpose (Node cannot spawn npm.cmd without a shell)

patches.title: A recorder that only worked on Windows, and said "no sessions" when it failed
patches.symptom: three recorders computed `.dsh/sessions` on Linux/macOS (`USERPROFILE` is unset there) and exited 3 with "no session directory"; an empty `DSH_SESSIONS=` was accepted as the root, pointing them at the current directory
patches.rootCause: `process.env.USERPROFILE ?? join(...)` turned "the variable is missing" into "the home is the empty string", and a join of an empty home is a relative path; the homedir-based recorder was the one that worked on both platforms
limits: not "runs on macOS": the POSIX branch it takes is the Linux one measured here
an empty HOME still cannot be resolved; the fallback is a literal ~/.dsh/sessions, not a lookup
the plugin never read USERPROFILE; only these offline recorders did

patches.title: The acceptance recorder owned a fixture count the package owns
patches.symptom: a green published package was recorded as a failed install: verify printed eight PASS lines and OK 8 fixture(s), and the recorder still answered "verify did not print OK 6 fixture(s)" because it looked for a literal six
patches.rootCause: R49 added two canonical fixtures, so the count became eight in three places and stayed six in a fourth: record_install_acceptance.mjs carried both a regex and a claimed string with the old number
limits: the criterion is the count plus every PASS line, not fixture contents: verify still owns what each case must decide
it cannot name the drifted fixture; sync_fixtures --check does
an npm exec that exits 0 with no output is still a failure

patches.title: The installed CLI was silent on Linux, and exited 0
patches.symptom: the installed bin printed nothing and exited 0 on Linux (and by the same code path on macOS), while node dist/cli.js verify printed the full result: the one command every acceptance and README quotes verified nothing
patches.rootCause: the entry guard compared import.meta.url with pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]), and npm installs a POSIX bin as a symlink, so the two differ and main() never ran; Windows installs a .cmd shim with the real path
limits: 0.4.11 carries the old guard: the fix ships in 0.4.12, and 0.4.11 stays installable but silent through its bin
the fix makes the command run; it adds no output of its own

patches.title: The profile and the refusal never met, and the seam cannot move the level
patches.symptom: the host refused `reasoningEffort: xhigh` 37 times on one route while the profile still fixed it: the census had the count and the profile had the level, and nothing compared them
patches.rootCause: P-0013 named the class and `scan` counted it by code, but the level lived only inside the host sentence; `agent/pre-step` `enter` cannot change a selection the loop fixed, and `reject` is disqualified on desktop
limits: it names the conflict and exits 1; only changing the profile stops the next dead turn, and it never clamps
a profile that omits reasoningEffort produces no finding, even when the UI selected a refused level

patches.title: The guard written for a fixture could not see it
patches.symptom: the 0.4.13 tarball carries this machine's account name in `fixtures/toolcall-fusion/bare-code-value.json`, and the P-0028 guard written for that file was green on it
patches.rootCause: the guard allowed two separators before `Users`, but the fixture is a JSON string, so one backslash becomes four; a second artifact leaked the name as a bare `ls -l` token no path rule sees
limits: the 0.4.13 tarball still carries the name: a published version is fixed forward, not rewritten
the guard runs after the fact; the writer knows only path shapes

patches.title: A truncated turn was counted, and nobody asked whether it answered
patches.symptom: `scan` reported 88 `max-tokens` turns on this machine and none of them said whether the user saw anything; 88 of them ended with no text and no tool call (upstream #12347 recorded the empty final answer on a headless run)
patches.rootCause: the census reads `turn/end` only, and `assistant/message` carries the block types that answer the second half of the question; nothing in `session-scan.ts` had ever looked at one
limits: it does not repair, retry or re-end a truncation; the host decides when to stop
it counts `max_tokens` only: a `completed` turn with only reasoning is upstream #13169 and needs its own evidence
a partial text counts as answered, because the user saw words; whether they were useful is not provable here

patches.title: A refusal thrown before the stream starts never reaches the seam that names it
patches.symptom: a requested effort the adapter does not map dies in prepareCall with UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT; the loop catch emits `agent/error` (never `agent/request-error`), so a listener on the latter alone names nothing (37 such turns on this host)
patches.rootCause: `agent/request-error` is dispatched only after a started stream fails (dsh-agent-loop line 942); prepareCall throws before that and the loop catch emits `agent/error` instead (line 657)
limits: `agent/error` has no decision: it names a failure and cannot retry or change the turn
one `(turn, step, code)` set is shared with `agent/request-error`, so a failure both seams see is named once
one route measured; another adapter may throw the refusal after opening a stream

patches.title: The first screens were one patch short and one release behind
patches.symptom: both READMEs claimed forty-four patches and enumerated the tested ones, but P-0043 appeared in neither; both also put 0.4.14 first under a status sentence calling 0.4.15 published
patches.rootCause: gate_copy checks numbers, bytes and provenance, not completeness: nothing asked whether a page that advertises the count names every patch
limits: it reads ids, not sentences: a patch named in a wrong row still satisfies the rule (presence, not placement)
it pins only the published version; an unpublished release's numbers stay the fact pack's business
the status sentence is parsed with two fixed shapes, so a rewrite must keep one of them
it cannot see the two npm package pages: they carry no enumeration, so the rule is vacuous there

patches.title: A turn that finished without answering anyone was never counted
patches.symptom: P-0044 counted truncations that answered nobody and left the other ending out: a `completed` turn whose last message is one `reasoning` block (upstream #13169) produced 0 cases here, so nothing in the scanner could even say whether it happened
patches.rootCause: the census asks how a turn ended and the answer rule asks what the last step showed, but only the max-tokens branch joined them; the adapter guard counts blocks rather than usable content, so a reasoning-only message passes as a normal stop
limits: it counts `completed` only: an error already names its code and an abort was the operator decision
a reasoning block a client renders to the user still counts as no answer: the rule is what the transcript gives a reader
the adapter guard that lets the shape through is upstream; this patch names the consequence, it does not repair it

patches.title: The platform boundary was prose, and prose is not a criterion
patches.symptom: every page said macOS not measured while the workflow had two jobs, so no darwin process ran the suite and a darwin-only break would land green
patches.rootCause: the sentence described a CI that did not exist: nothing recorded which platforms run, so not measured meant three different things
limits: CI is not a host: no `data/results/live-*`, so no patch may claim `verified` on it
it proves the suite and gates pass on darwin, not that the desktop app mounts there
weaker than the hand-run Linux evidence, which also measures the byte account and the installed bin
the first push that carries it is the measurement

patches.title: The pack counted a project it no longer described
patches.symptom: the pack said 41 patches against 48, named P-0013 on the seam P-0045 moved it off, listed 8 CLI and 21 build-side ids against 10 and 24, and CHANGELOG stopped at 0.4.15 while 0.4.16 shipped
patches.rootCause: gate_copy compares outward files with the pack and facts-truth read four claims: nothing compared the pack with the registry
limits: presence and counts, not placement: the prose beside an id is not read
the census is parsed from the bullet shape used today, so a rewrite turns the rule red rather than wrong
changelog headers are read, not contents; the published version stays the pack own claim

patches.title: A resumed session can lose a tool it already called, and nothing counted it
patches.symptom: upstream #12348: a resume stops declaring a tool this session used and the host answers UNKNOWN_TOOL; nothing read a request/header here
patches.rootCause: scan read attempts, turns and codes, never request/header, so no rule compared a header with what the session had already called
limits: it proves the request set lost a tool the session used, not what the model remembers
a drop nobody called, and a call made only after the drop, are both refused
it counts resume and change alike, cannot see a provider that sends no header, and names no verdict
